**Stable, published under the npm `latest` dist-tag.** A plain
`npx @candid-core/cli` runs this version once it is published; `beta` stays on
0.2.0-beta.1. Until 1.0, any release may change the CLI grammar, the library
API, and the request/response shapes. Pin an exact version.

`@candid-core/schema` 0.3 breaks the 0.2 API (principal values are canonical text, collapsing opts are boxed, every `vec nat8` is a `Uint8Array`, generated modules use a new binding layout and may omit declarations, and the `./actor`, `./transport-icp`, `./forms` and `./labels` subpaths are gone); there is no compatibility layer.

That line is the 0.3 line's, unchanged. What this release breaks against
0.2.0 is below.

## Installation

```sh
npm install --save-exact @candid-core/schema@0.4.0
npm install --save-dev --save-exact @candid-core/cli@0.3.0
npx @candid-core/cli@0.3.0 gen ./service.did -o ./generated
```

## What an app on 0.3.0 / 0.2.0 does

1. Move both packages in one step, each at its exact version, with the two
   install lines above. This release's peer is exactly
   `@candid-core/schema` `0.4.0`; npm refuses a mismatched pair (`ERESOLVE
   could not resolve`, as measured for the 0.3.0 pair with npm 11.3.0).
2. Run `gen` again over every committed module, then `gen --check` in CI as
   before. A module 0.2.0 wrote differs from what this release writes for
   the same `.did`, so `gen --check` reports it as `drifted` and exits 1
   until it is regenerated; the envelope beside it is byte-identical and is
   reported `unchanged`.
3. Fix what the compiler reports, which for code that imports the generated
   names is nothing, with one exception: a type-level test comparing a
   method type of `Actor` for exact equality with its bare call signature
   now sees `& $.WithMode<mode>`.

The two orders that do not work: CLI 0.3.0's modules against schema 0.3.0
fail to compile (`TS2694`, below), and schema 0.4.0 beside CLI 0.2.0 does
not install (CLI 0.2.0 peers exactly `0.3.0`). A module CLI 0.2.0 wrote does
compile against schema 0.4.0.
[Migrating from 0.3.0](https://b3hr4d.github.io/candid-core/migrating-from-0-3.html)
has the same steps, with the compiler's errors.

## Pairing

- **Peer**: `@candid-core/schema` at exactly `0.4.0` (optional, as before;
  exactly `0.3.0` in 0.2.0). Each method of a generated module's `Actor` is
  typed with `$.WithMode`, which 0.4.0 adds: against 0.3.0 a module with an
  actor method fails with `TS2694` ("Namespace … has no exported member
  'WithMode'"), once per method. The schema release is published first.
- **Embedded revision**: `candid-core` 0.1.0-beta.3 and the `candid-core-ts`
  generator, both compiled from the commit the release is dispatched from;
  the run records the SHA, and the release record below names it on publish
  day. This release is prepared on `main` at
  `2358784082bc26d04c40d75ac90f0a10e9e3bd07` (#246 merged), and the
  dispatch commit is the merge of the pull request that bumps the versions,
  which changes no Rust or generator file. That commit's `candid-core`
  source is ahead of the crates.io 0.1.0-beta.3 archive by five changes not
  yet in a crate release: the four 0.2.0 carried (a leading UTF-8 byte
  order mark accepted, #176, #177; a run of more than 256 consecutive
  comments refused, #219; a type on a cycle through `opt` alone refused,
  #234; a struct written as a JSON array refused by the Contract loaders,
  #235) and, since 0.2.0, a unit variant written as a JSON map refused by
  the Contract loaders (#238, #243). No input of this package reaches the
  last two: `gen`, `project`, `check`, `didToContract`, `didToModule`,
  `projectDid` and `checkCompatible` read `.did` sources and never load a
  Contract document. Inputs both accept produce the same Contract and
  identities, and the envelopes' `producer` still reads `0.1.0-beta.3`.
- **Not released with it**: the `candid-core` crate. crates.io stays on
  0.1.0-beta.3; no crate release was asked for, and none is needed, since
  no Contract or identity moved. The root changelog records the five
  changes under `## Unreleased` for the next crate release.

## Public API against 0.2.0

The previous stable release. Library (`lib/index.d.ts`, against 0.2.0's
`gitHead`, `acabe0fcfbd8019d14e2c2550c5e6cd872a3529a`). The registry's 0.2.0
tarball (shasum `0c90f2f9b5eeac839433ca4b322ca701bbe83ca3`, equal to
`npm view @candid-core/cli@0.2.0 dist.shasum`) holds `lib/index.d.ts`,
`lib/index.js`, `bin/cli.js`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` byte-identical
to that `gitHead`; its wasm needs the release toolchain to rebuild, so the
tarball's integrity was not reproduced. Against it, every declaration of
`lib/index.d.ts` is kept with identical text, and the file only gains
declarations.

| Name | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `projectDid(sources, methods)` | added |
| `checkCompatible(written, live)` | added |
| `Identities`, `ProjectionSuccess`, `CompatibilityDiagnostic`, `CompatibilityReport`, `CheckFailure` | added |
| `init`, `didToContract`, `didToModule`, `Sources`, `SourceSpan`, `RelatedLocation`, `ResourceLimitInfo`, `Diagnostic`, `Failure`, `FieldNameTriple`, `ContractEnvelope`, `ModuleSuccess`, `Omission`, `CliReport`, `CliEntryReport`, `CliEntryStatus` | unchanged |
| `peerDependencies` | **BREAKING**, `@candid-core/schema` exactly `0.3.0` becomes exactly `0.4.0` |

Command line (each behaviour of this release measured from the packed
tarball, and of 0.2.0 from the registry's tarball, Node 24.2.0, macOS
arm64):

| 0.2.0 | 0.3.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `candid-core-cli gen <service.did>... [-o <dir>] [--json] [--check]` | unchanged |
| `project …` and `check …` exit 64 with the one-line usage | `candid-core-cli project <in.did> --methods <a,b,...> -o <out.did> [--json]` and `candid-core-cli check <written.did> --against <live.did> [--json]` (additive) |
| a usage error prints one usage line | a usage error prints three, one per command; still exit 64, stderr only |
| `gen` writes `type $X = …` and `type $Actor = { m: (…) => Promise<…> }` | **BREAKING** (module text): `export type X = …` and `m: ((…) => Promise<…>) & $.WithMode<"query">`; `gen --check` against 0.2.0's output exits 1 with `drifted` for the module, `unchanged` for the envelope |

Generated modules (the text this tool writes):

- **BREAKING**: each type is declared under its Candid name
  (`export type Account = …`), the schema bound as the local `$Account`
  and exported under the same name, as before. Every export name, and what
  each export is as a type and as a value, is unchanged, and so is each
  module's set of declarations. A name that cannot be a type in the module
  keeps the `$` local for its type too: the four global types the generated
  types use (`Array`, `Promise`, `Record`, `Uint8Array`) and 62 words
  TypeScript refuses as a type's name.
- **BREAKING**: each method of `Actor` is its call signature intersected
  with `$.WithMode<"query" | "composite_query" | "update" | "oneway">`,
  which needs `@candid-core/schema` 0.4.0. Call signatures, method names,
  `Parameters<>`, `ReturnType<>` and `keyof Actor` are unchanged, and a
  plain async function still implements a method.
- Measured on the repository's 41 tracked `.did` files: the 37 that both
  releases generate give a different module and a byte-identical envelope,
  and the 4 that 0.2.0 refuses this release refuses with the same exit
  status.

## Projection and compatibility (new)

- **`project`** writes a self-contained `.did` holding only the named methods
  and every declaration they reach, with declaration names, doc comments and
  argument names kept, and prints the interface identities of the input and
  of the projection. Deterministic for the same input and the same set of
  names. Its bounds: 1 MiB of output (`projection_bytes`) and 4 MiB of
  unknown-method diagnostics (`projection_diagnostic_bytes`). `-o` may not
  be, or become, a source of the input (`output_is_input`).
- **`check`** exits 0 when the live interface is still a Candid subtype of
  the written one, and 1 otherwise, with `method_missing`, `mode_changed`,
  `method_incompatible`, the warning `special_opt_rule`, and
  `resource_limit_exceeded` when a bound is reached: per method, 384 pairs on
  one path, 1,000,000 steps and 1,000 reported warnings; per check,
  10,000,000 steps (one more per method), 10,000 warnings and 4 MiB of
  reported diagnostics. A response is at most 4 MiB and 1,016 bytes. The
  check is tested against the subtype check of the `candid` crate it pins
  and against `@candid-core/schema`'s decoder; where that crate's
  coinductive memo accepts a pair that is not a subtype, this check
  refuses it, as the decoder does.
- The owner's three decisions on #249 (2026-10-10) ship as merged: the
  wasm crate depends on `candid_parser` `=0.4.0` (and on `candid`
  `=0.10.30` for its tests only), both already in the graph at those pins;
  past 1,000 warnings a method keeps its verdict; and `project` refuses an
  output that is, or would become, a source of the input.

## Known limitations and deferred work

- An entry named through a file symlink, or in another case on a
  case-insensitive file system, fails with `did_source_not_found` (#251).
  `gen`, `project` and `check` read an entry by the spelling the bundle
  walk lists. Name each entry as it is on disk.
- Compiling a `.did` with source info, which `gen`, `didToContract`,
  `didToModule`, `projectDid` and `checkCompatible` all do, takes time about
  quadratic in the number of record, variant, func and service types
  written, before the compiler's size limits are checked (#252). The
  `check` bounds above cover the walk, not the compile of each side.
- The multi-entry bundle-root rule and the duplicate-stem refusal apply the
  issue's recommendations and may be revisited before 1.0 (#193).
- Two structurally equal record declarations still collapse to the first
  name (#197, "Not yet scheduled"), and declarations whose records
  canonicalize to one node share its field names (#229).
- The embedded `candid-core` is not byte-identical to any crates.io release
  (above); the next crate release carries all five changes, which the root
  changelog already records under `## Unreleased`.

## Irreversibility

An npm version number is permanent: once published it can be deprecated, but
never republished with other bytes. The wasm in the tarball is built in the
release job with the pinned release toolchain and `wasm-pack`, so its bytes
are those two pins applied to the dispatched commit.
